title: Cap. 7 Contra Obj. 2: merits applied before faith?
pass_a_gloss: If we posit that the elect obtain efficacious grace, or saving faith, from the fact that the death and merit of Christ suffering on the cross was being applied to them by a certain special intention, then we seem to admit the merits of Christ's passion imputed or applied to certain human beings before their faith: But this stands against the received opinion of the theologians, which posits that faith is the instrument or medium without which the merits of Christ's passion are not applied to singular persons: It is necessary therefore that he stand actually faithful who has Christ's merits singularly applied or imputed to himself. How then can this special application of Christ's merits to the elect, not yet made faithful and believing, be defended?
pass_b_english: Suppose the elect gain efficacious grace — saving faith — because Christ's death and merit on the cross were applied to them by a special intention. Then we seem to allow the merits of his passion to be imputed or applied to some people before they believe. That clashes with the received theological rule that faith is the instrument or means without which Christ's passion-merits are not applied to particular persons. So whoever has Christ's merits singularly applied or imputed must already stand as a believer. How then can we defend this special application of Christ's merits to the elect before they are made faithful and believing?
source_text: Si ponamus electos obtinere gratiam efficacem, sive fidem salutiferam, exinde quod mors meritumque Christi in cruce patientis speciali quadam intentione illis applicabatur, tum videmur admittere merita passionis Christi quibusdam hominibus imputata sive applicata ante fidem ipsorum: At hoc receptae Theologorum sententiae adversatur, quae ponit fidem esse instrumentum sive medium, sine quo merita passionis Christi singularibus personis non applicantur: Necesse est igitur ut is actu fidelis exstet, qui Christi merita habeat sibi singulariter applicata aut imputata. Quomodo igitur defendi potest specialis haec applicatio meritorum Christi ad electos, nondum factos fideles & credentes?
